description:
This is a 6 month fixed term contract initially, with a strong likelihood of extention.

DEPT® is a Growth Invention company built to help the world’s most ambitious brands grow faster. Operating at the intersection of technology and marketing, our 4,000+ specialists deliver growth invention services across Brand & Media, Experience, Commerce, CRM, and Technology & Data. We’re 50|50 tech and marketing, partner-led, and first to move. Clients include Google, Lufthansa, Meta, eBay, and OpenAI. We have been certified B Corp and Climate Neutral since 2021.

JOB PURPOSE

This role is part of our Global Studios team. We create emotive yet conversion-focused ideas, products and campaigns at scale and speed. Our specialty is hyper-personalised, digital communications that change perceptions, shape new behaviours, and shift market share for our clients.

As Account Director, you will be responsible for building strong relationships with clients at all levels including strategic input, and overseeing the delivery of a wide variety of substantial integrated campaigns.

You will be required to manage client briefs from start to finish, planning, assigning and reviewing creative and managing the overall agency workload in partnership with the producers and the senior design team. 

You will be working closely with designers, copywriters, developers and other parts of the agency to ensure successful campaign deliveries which are profitable without compromising creative integrity.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Manage client briefs from start to finish, ensuring successful delivery to client deadlines across multiple campaigns. 
  • Liaise with clients and manage their expectations. 
  • Re-lay client feedback to designers, copywriters and developers & plan and manage workloads of the team.
  • Ensure client requirements are met whilst protecting DEPT® values/brand.
  • Support the senior team with administrative tasks.
  • Build a full understanding of the clients’ business, strategies, objectives, brand, audiences and challenges, advising on the communications solution that best meets their needs, with a view to becoming their trusted adviser.
  • Build excellent working relationships with key clients – regular meetings, planning, briefing, evaluation.
  • Work closely with creative and strategy teams and to have oversight of all statements of work/proposals as well as all content production for clients.
  • Ensure the right DEPT® team is in place to deliver, high standards are maintained and adding value wherever possible. Ensure success criteria are met and projects are delivered to time and to budget.
  • Ensure a good knowledge of all DEPT® products and services and actively promote them to clients.
  • Report to senior management with internal and external issues and events that might impact upon accounts, either positively or negatively.
  • Direct account management activity – undertaking pitches and presentations, formulating and implementing account plans, and running the account management process.
  • Hold key new business development responsibilities, working with others in the team to proactively seek new opportunities for the business. Writing proposals and creative treatment. Contributing to winning new business.
  • Ensure processes are followed and that there is consistent professional delivery (to brief). Managing workflows. Lead Account Direction best practice within the Agency.
  • Maintain a strategic overview of key accounts and their markets – running regular internal client-facing account reviews. To prove how we are meeting our clients’ objectives through metrics, feedback, research, etc.
  • Oversee the client contract, to proactively manage the account and resources to maximise profitability.

Management and leadership

  • Delegate and allocate responsibilities efficiently to manage projects end to end. 
  • Interview candidates and hire resources.
  • Conduct performance reviews of team members and identify areas of improvement, give feedback and recommend for promotions or salary increments.
  • Effectively lead teams and inspire others to achieve goals through innovation, quality and excellence.
  • Identify strengths and weaknesses of team members and suitably make changes if required. 
  • Encourage team interaction, boost employee motivation and appreciate team contribution. 
  • Match project tasks with opportunities for development so that employee potential is utilised to the maximum.
  • Manage change and effectively cascade information to teams to ensure smooth execution.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • Experience delivering a broad range of multi-channel marketing communications including digital and direct.
  • Extremely organised, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet and manage deadlines with ease and efficiency.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • A great team player and team-building skills.
  • People management/leadership skills.
  • Excellent negotiator with good networking ability. 
  • Ability to communicate effectively with team giving guidance and feedback. 
  • Resource management skills and ability to handle complex issues. 
  • Understanding of the production & interactive processes.
  • Excellent planning and organisation skills.
  • Ability to manage and develop client and supplier relationships. 
  • Ability to commercially manage budgets. 
  • Proven business development experience and success.
  • Advanced working knowledge of Microsoft Office Packages.

WE OFFER

  • A flexible hybrid working policy to enjoy the best of both worlds (2 days from the office, depending on location).
  • Early Finish Fridays, kickstart your weekend early with alternating early-finish Fridays.
  • 26 days paid holiday, plus UK Bank Holidays.
  • Access to dedicated mental health resources including enhanced sick pay scheme, employee assistance programme and trained Mental Health First Aiders. 
  • Company Pension Scheme. 
  • Access to a Private Medical Insurance or Cash Plan scheme. 
  • Season Ticket Loan, interest-free Season Ticket Loans to help spread the cost of travel.
  • Cycle to Work Scheme, save money on a new bike and equipment.

Our Mission: Why Lighthouse? 

At Lighthouse, we’re on a mission to revolutionize commercial strategy as hospitality’s most powerful AI platform. We take the world's largest hotel data network and transform it into real-time intelligence that drives action. We don't just deliver insights; we empower businesses to make decisions that move revenue. 

With $370M in Series C funding and over $100M in ARR, we are scaling at lightspeed. Our 850+ teammates across 35 countries aren't just building software—they are leveraging cutting-edge AI to help hoteliers be the first to act. Tens of thousands of hotels across 185 countries trust Lighthouse to execute their commercial strategy, including every one of the top 15 global chains and thousands of independent hotels that consistently outperform their markets. With Lighthouse AI, the intelligence gets deeper. Decisions get smarter. Actions get faster. We help hoteliers be first to act.

Lighthouse Values: Our guiding light

We are Lumineers. Our shared values keep us on a collaborative path fostering a cultural and customer centric environment

  • Pursuit of greatness: We’re innovators who care deeply about our customers’ success. Our team brings their best work, stays curious, and delivers excellence through attention to detail
  • Meaningful work matters: We make every moment count by knowing what to deliver, why it matters, and how it drives Lighthouse forward
  • Elevate each other: We don’t just work together - we grow together. What unites us is understanding each other as people and working toward shared goals

We’re more than just a workplace – we’re a community. Collaborative, fun, and deeply committed, we work hard together to revolutionize the hospitality sector. Are you ready to join us and shine brighter in the industry’s most exciting rocket-ship? 🚀

Job details

● 💼 Revenue Team
● 📍 United Kingdom 
● 🕜 Full-Time - Remote


What you will do 

You’ll be the face of Lighthouse for our most strategic prospects, owning complex, multi-stakeholder deal cycles from prospecting to close. This is a senior hunter role: you carry a significant quota, you build your own pipeline, and you’re accountable to outcomes and success. No excuses, just results. 

What makes this different: you won’t do it alone. Lighthouse is deploying an agent AI infrastructure — Enablement, Pre-Sales, and Coaching agents — alongside a modern revenue stack. AI handles the prep, the sequencing, and the pattern recognition so you can focus on what matters — building relationships, running sharp discovery, and closing deals. 

Where you will have impact 

Own your territory and your number. Build and execute a strategic territory plan targeting high value and enterprise accounts. Maintain 3x pipeline coverage, forecast honestly, and take full accountability for your results. Your quota is your commitment.

Hunt and build a pipeline. Source a meaningful share of your own pipeline through outbound sequences, ICP targeting, your existing network, Lighthouse Connect events, and industry conferences. Activate relationships from prior roles and industry tenure. This is not an SDR-reliant role. 

Run a disciplined sales process. Using MEDDPICC to qualify and advance opportunities. Use the AI Pre-Sales Agent to identify gaps before every major call. Navigate complex deal cycles with multiple stakeholders and longer timelines. Advance deals through stage gates with evidence, not optimism. Leverage AI to make your days easier and focus on more selling time. 

Use AI as a force multiplier. Leverage the Enablement Agent for call prep, discovery frameworks, and positioning. Use the Coaching Agent to surface patterns in your pipeline and win rate. Push back on the tools when they’re wrong — help make the system smarter. 

Become a hospitality expert. Understand the commercial challenges hotels face across pricing, distribution, and business intelligence. Position Lighthouse’s full platform as the integrated solution that replaces fragmented point tools. Know the competitive landscape inside out and run value based ROI conversations confidently. 

Drive results beyond net-new. Consistently meet and exceed sales targets through new business and by identifying expansion and upgrade opportunities within your accounts. Partner with Product to share market feedback and influence the roadmap. Represent Lighthouse at industry events to build the brand and your network. 

Elevate the team around you. Share deal strategies, competitive insights, and best practices with the broader AE team. Informally mentor newer reps and contribute to playbooks and enablement content. This isn’t a management role, but leadership is expected. 

About Our Team 

You’ll join a global Revenue team of 150+ sales professionals across 24 countries. Our team works across the full Lighthouse product suite, helping hotels, chains, and hospitality groups achieve their commercial goals. It’s a collaborative, high-energy environment with real opportunities for career growth and the chance to learn from experienced leaders as we continue to expand our market share. 

What’s in it for you

  • Flexible working environment: Work from home or at one of our global offices.
  • Comprehensive health insurance: Private AXA coverage for you and your family.
  • Flexible time off: Autonomy to manage your work-life balance.
  • Competitive compensation: Proactively maintained to value your work.
  • Collaborative team: High-bar, friendly, creative, and passionate colleagues.
  • Career development: Workshops and frameworks to realize your full potential.
  • Impactful work: Shape products relied on by 85,000+ users worldwide.
  • Wellbeing support: Subsidized up to 80% ClassPass subscription.
  • Referral bonuses: Earn rewards for bringing in new talent.
  • Additional maternity leave compensation: For the first 12 weeks of Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), we top-up your SMP so that your salary reaches 100%.

Who You Are 

  • 3+ years in a closing sales role with a consistent track record of hitting or exceeding quota. SaaS experience is essential; hospitality tech is a strong advantage. 
  • Self-directed, coachable, and driven to continuously improve. You seek feedback on your calls, your pipeline, and your positioning — and act on it within the next deal, not the next quarter. 
  • You treat AI tools as a core part of your selling motion, not a novelty. You adopt new tooling quickly and bend it to your style. 
  • You’ve worked with MEDDPICC or similar qualification frameworks and can demonstrate how structured deal execution has driven your results.
  • Strong business acumen with the ability to sell on value, not price. Confident engaging stakeholders from GMs to C-suite and navigating complex buying committees. 
  • You want to win. You prospect when it would be easier not to. You follow up one more time. You’re not okay with a bad quarter.

Diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging

Thank you for considering a career with Lighthouse. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace that values equal opportunity for all. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds, regardless of age, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, and disability. Our commitment to equality is part of our culture. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point during the application or interview process, please notify your recruiter.

Not ticking every box? No problem! We value diverse backgrounds and unique skill sets, and we encourage individuals from all walks of life to apply. If your experience looks a little different from what we've described, but you're passionate about what we do and are a quick learner, we'd love to hear from you!

Pourquoi Deliveroo ?

Nous transformons la façon dont le monde mange et fait ses courses en rendant leur accès plus pratique et agréable. Nous connectons les consommateurs, les restaurants, les magasins et les cyclistes. Nous donnons à chaque personne la possibilité d'acheter ce qu'elles veulent, comme elles le veulent, quand elles le veulent et où elles le veulent.

Nous sommes une entreprise axée sur la technologie, à l'avant-garde d’un secteur qui connaît une des expansions les plus rapides au monde. Nous avançons rapidement, valorisons l'autonomie, et sommes toujours en recherche de nouvelles idées et de personnes talentueuses pour nous rejoindre!

Tes principales missions :  

  • Gérer un portefeuille de restaurants clés sur des zones matures, où l’expertise et l’attention au détail font toute la différence.
  • Développer des partenariats privilégiés et durables en devenant le point de contact expert de votre zone et en mettant à profit vos connaissances Food Tech.
  • Optimiser la performance de vos comptes grâce à un accompagnement personnalisé, construit sur le long terme et nourri par la data.
  • Analyser les résultats de vos restaurants, identifier les leviers d’amélioration et recommander des actions concrètes à votre manager tout en restant agile et ouvert à la nouveauté.
  • Proposer et mettre en place des campagnes marketing et promotionnelles ciblées pour booster l’attractivité de vos restaurants partenaires.
  • Suivre de près le déroulé des opérations afin de garantir la meilleure expérience restaurant et client possible.

Ton expérience et tes qualités :

  • Tu as déjà 2 à 3 ans d’expérience sur un rôle similaire où la gestion d’un portefeuille de partenaires était centrale à ta mission.
  • Tu sais négocier et anticiper les discussions commerciales tout en gardant à l’esprit les valeurs de Deliveroo.
  • Tu sais garder le contrôle de ton portefeuille, identifier les nouvelles tendances du marché et partager du feedback utile à tes partenaires ainsi qu’à ton manager.
  • Le terrain est un lieu où tu te sens à ta place : tu sais construire des relations de confiance avec tes partenaires tout en gardant un œil attentif sur la concurrence.
  • Tu sais te montrer proactif, analyser les résultats de tes actions et proposer des recommandations concrètes à ton manager.
  • Tu travailles de manière autonome tout en gardant le cap fixé, sais t’approprier des objectifs précis et mets tout en œuvre pour les atteindre.
  • Tu sais concevoir des actions spécifiques, adaptées à la fois aux besoins de tes partenaires et à la stratégie définie par ton manager.
  • Tu sais identifier, comprendre et analyser les données de performance (commerciales et opérationnelles) pour garantir un niveau de service irréprochable.
  • Tu sais t’exprimer en anglais (à l’oral comme à l’écrit)
  • Tu arrives à convaincre tout en construisant des relations commerciales solides, durables, où Deliveroo devient le partenaire de choix
  • Et si tu cherches un poste où tu travailles en full remote depuis Lille, tout en gardant un lien fort avec le terrain et les équipes, alors c’est peut‑être le rôle qu’il te faut !

La vie chez Deliveroo

Notre équipe est en forte croissance, notre impact très important, et nous cherchons à répondre aux questions les plus stimulantes du moment. Nous progressons rapidement, nous explorons toujours de nouvelles idées et nous sommes très transparents quant aux décisions que nous prenons et à ce qui motive nos choix.

Il y a tellement de questions que nous souhaitons résoudre, et encore plus que nous n'avons pas encore rencontrées. Comment les données et la technologie peuvent-elles aider les restaurants à développer leur activité à mesure que les habitudes des consommateurs évoluent ? Comment pouvons-nous prédire ce qu'une personne souhaitera pour dîner avant même que l'idée ne lui vienne à l'esprit ? Chez Deliveroo, ces questions ne sont que quelques-uns des défis ambitieux auxquels nous nous efforçons de répondre – et il n'y a aucun projet qui ne peut pas devenir le vôtre. Aucune solution n'appartient à une équipe en particulier, ce qui vous ouvre d'extraordinaires possibilités en termes de développement et d'impact personnel.

Avantages et diversité

À compétences égales, ce poste est ouvert aux travailleurs et travailleuses en situation de handicap ou assimilés au sens de l’article L5212-13 du Code du travail. Deliveroo s’engage en faveur de la diversité, l’égalité professionnelle, l’emploi des personnes en situation de handicap.

Deliveroo France valorise la diversité sans discrimination de genre, race, sexualité, religion ou préférences personnelles. Avec un score de 99/100 à l'Indice de l'Égalité Hommes-Femmes 2023, nous sommes engagés envers l'égalité des chances. Rejoignez-nous avec votre passion pour la nourriture dans une entreprise en pleine croissance.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

We’ll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

Looking for a role where Finance meets Supply Chain Operations? 

At Infinitesima, we're building advanced metrology systems used by the world's leading semiconductor manufacturers to produce next-generation computer chips. Our technology helps enable the devices people rely on every day, from smartphones to AI infrastructure.  

As we continue to grow, we're looking for an Accounts & Supply Chain Administrator to join our team in Abingdon. This is more than a typical accounts support role.  

 

What We're Looking For

This role would suit someone who already has experience in a purchasing, supply chain, ERP administration, accounts payable or operations support environment and can quickly become productive with minimal supervision.

You'll need to enjoy working independently, following established processes and taking ownership of a high-volume administrative workload. This is not a role where you'll be constantly directed day-to-day, so you'll need the confidence to manage priorities, solve routine problems and proactively chase colleagues for the information needed to keep orders, invoices and transactions moving.

Essential

  • Previous experience in a purchasing, supply chain, ERP administration, accounts payable or similar operational support role
  • Strong Microsoft Excel and spreadsheet skills
  • Excellent numerical accuracy and attention to detail
  • Confident working with large volumes of data entry and data validation
  • Comfortable following established processes accurately and consistently
  • Able to work independently and hit the ground running with minimal training
  • Confident communicating with colleagues at all levels of the business
  • Comfortable persistently following up and chasing stakeholders for information, approvals and updates when required
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously
  • A proactive, self-sufficient approach with a willingness to take ownership of tasks

Desirable

  • Experience using WinMan ERP, or a similar ERP/MRP system such as SAP, Oracle, Epicor, NetSuite or Microsoft Dynamics
  • Understanding of purchasing processes, purchase orders, goods receipting and supplier management
  • Experience processing supplier invoices and reconciling transactions
  • Previous experience supporting both Supply Chain and Finance functions
  • Experience maintaining accurate inventory, purchasing or operational records within an ERP system

A Note About This Role

We're keen to be transparent about the nature of the position.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys structured work, maintaining accurate records, processing transactions, and ensuring data quality within business systems. A significant proportion of your time will be spent entering, checking and validating information within our ERP and finance systems.

Success in this role comes from being thorough, organised and persistent rather than constantly seeking new projects. You'll enjoy this opportunity if you take pride in accuracy, process compliance and keeping the business running smoothly behind the scenes.

While you will gain exposure to both Finance and Supply Chain activities, this is not intended to be a fast-track management or leadership role, and progression opportunities are likely to be limited. We are therefore looking for someone who enjoys this type of operational work and is motivated by doing it well rather than viewing it as a stepping stone to another position.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Manage the accurate processing of supplier invoices and purchasing transactions
  • Maintain data integrity within WinMan and other business systems
  • Create, update and validate purchasing, inventory and supplier records
  • Follow up with engineers, managers and other stakeholders to obtain missing information and approvals
  • Resolve discrepancies between purchase orders, goods receipts and supplier invoices
  • Produce and maintain accurate records and audit trails
  • Support the smooth operation of the Supply Chain and Finance functions through accurate and timely administration
  • Help improve process efficiency and data quality as the business grows

Interested? 

If you're organised, detail-focused and enjoy bringing order to complex processes, we'd love to hear from you. 

A bit about us: 
Infinitesima is a privately owned company founded in 2001, as a spin-out of the University of Bristol, by CTO Professor Andrew Humphris. Our dynamic team of scientists and engineers is focussed on enabling the next generation of semiconductor devices through delivery of innovative products to customers around the world.

1st stage: (45 minute) Remote meeting to evaluate your experience and technical ability 

2nd stage: (2.5 hours) Face to face onsite evaluating technical, presentation and communication skills along with your ways of working and your opportunity to gt to know more about us

We use AI only to transcribe our interviews so we can focus fully on you instead of scribbling notes. The AI does not take part in any decision making at any stage. All hiring decisions are made by real humans based on the conversation we have with you.

All of our new UK team members are asked to work on site here at Abingdon during their first three months with us. We offer flexible, hybrid working where possible upon completion of probation. This tends to be limited to Friday's due to the nature of the role which requires access to secure, onsite systems.

  • Experience running automated tests on BrowserStack (or a similar cloud device platform). 
  • Experience running automated tests on CI/CD pipelines (e.g. Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Bitrise, CircleCI). 
  • A methodical, quality-first mindset with strong attention to detail and a knack for spotting edge cases. 
  • Good communication skills and comfort collaborating across engineering, QE, and product functions. 

Preferred Skills:

  • Meaningful hands-on experience automating and testing native mobile applications (iOS and/or Android).

description:
🧡 About Alma

At Alma, we believe sustainable commerce depends on fair, well-balanced trade. Because finance plays a pivotal role in business, our mission is to put it back in its rightful place — serving merchants and consumers.

Our installment and deferred payment solutions help merchants boost sales by 20% or more, increase customer loyalty, and deliver a seamless shopping experience — without encouraging bad debt.

As the buy now pay later leader in France and active in 10 European countries, we've empowered over +25,000 merchants and 10 million consumers.

With 380+ Almakers and €100M+ ARR in 2025, Alma is scaling rapidly across Europe as a member of the Next40, and we're just getting started!

👐 About the team

Alma is a lender. We originate several million consumer receivables a year, carry them for a few weeks, and refinance them off a deliberately light balance sheet through securitization vehicles (Fonds Communs de Titrisation) and our other funding lines. We are regulated as a société de financement and a payment institution.

That changes what "accounting" means here. A lender's accounts are not a monthly deliverable produced at the end of a chain: they are the chain. Every payment event, every commission, every provision, every sale of receivables to an FCT has to become a journal entry that ties — to the transaction underneath it, to the general ledger above it, and to the prudential statements the regulator reads. At our scale and growth, this is a strategic topic, and one that is as much about data as it is about accounting.

Today the chain exists: an internal core banking ledger we built ourselves, feeding NetSuite, feeding regulatory reporting. What it does not have is a single owner who understands it end-to-end, holds it to the standard a regulated lender needs, and evolves it as the business changes (geographies, products, licenses). That is the role we are opening.

You will join an Accounting team inside a Finance organization of ~15 people covering Strategic Financing, FP&A, Accounting, Regulatory reporting and Controlling. You will report to the Head of Financing & Accounting, alongside the Financing team and the General Accounting Manager, who oversees corporate cycles, tax, statutory and consolidated accounts.

This is a role with unusual ownership for its level: the banking accounting scope is yours from day one, and so is the data chain that produces it.

💼 About the job

Own the accounting of the credit business:

  • Own how the portfolio is represented in the books: origination, revenue recognition on merchant and customer commissions, deferred income, write-offs and recoveries, cost of risk and provisioning on performing and non-performing exposures.
  • Own the accounting of our securitizations: sales of receivables to the FCTs, derecognition, discount and over-collateralisation, residual interests, servicing and management fees, hedging.
  • Own the accounting of our funding: corporate debt, commercial paper, and the new funding instruments we add as the refinancing strategy evolves.

Own the core banking ledger:

  • Be the functional owner of the engine that turns business events into accounting: which event, which account, which currency, which date, which counterparty.
  • Specify and validate the accounting schemes for every new product, partner and geography, and work with Engineering and Data on the ledger's model, its feed into the ERP, and the fixes when something drifts.
  • Own the audit trail end-to-end — from a single €40 installment to a line in a prudential statement — and make it documented enough to be walked through by someone whose job is to challenge it.

Reinforce the control framework:

  • Design and automate the reconciliations that hold the whole thing together: ledger ↔ general ledger ↔ bank ↔ FCT reporting ↔ prudential statements.
  • Shorten monthly close, incl. turning a manual, end-of-month, spreadsheet-based check into an automated, evidenced, repeatable control.
  • Be Finance's counterpart to Internal Control and Periodic Control on everything accounting-data related.

Own regulatory reporting:

  • Own the production and the quality of our prudential and statistical reporting — solvency, large exposures, liquidity, and the statistical returns that go with them.
  • Own the reconciliation tables that matter most: prudential statements to accounting balances, regulatory returns to the trial balance, own funds and RWA back to their audit trail.
  • Own the reporting tooling and its data feeds, and work with the Regulatory and Financing teams on the evolutions of the prudential framework and on the treatment of our securitizations.

🧩 About you

To succeed in this job:

  • You have around 6-7 years of experience, ideally starting in audit of financial services — banks, consumer credit, asset management, securitization — in a Big 4 or a specialised practice, possibly with a first move in-house. You know how to build a number, prove it, and defend it line by line in front of people whose job is to challenge it.
  • You know banking accounting for real: French banking GAAP, the PCEC, cost of risk, revenue recognition on credit products. Or you know financial services accounting well enough that the banking layer is a matter of months, not years.
  • You actually enjoy controls at scale — reconciling large populations, hunting the anomaly, chasing the last twelve euros of a four-hundred-million balance until you know exactly where they went. If that sounds tedious rather than satisfying, this is not your role.
  • You are autonomous and scrappy. On things to build, or on things that already exist.
  • You are fluent in English and French — our documentation and our regulator are French, part of our business and our team are not.

And it will be nice if you also:

  • Hold, or are working towards, the DEC (or CPA, ACCA, equivalent).
  • Have been exposed to securitization — FCTs, SPVs, waterfalls, deconsolidation — or to a regulated credit institution from the inside.
  • You are autonomous on data. SQL is a daily tool, a data warehouse does not intimidate you, and your reflex in front of a five-million-row population is to query it, not to ask someone for a summary. This is the single most important line in this job description.
  • Know NetSuite, BigQuery, dbt or Python.
  • Have worked in a scaling fintech.

Don't meet every single requirement? At Alma, we believe great hires come from diverse paths. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply. We value potential, curiosity and the ability to grow as much as experience.

🤑 Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive salary based on 12 months
  • Profit-sharing and employee savings plan
  • Health insurance: 100% covered by Alma including family package
  • Disability insurance: 100% covered by Alma
  • Sport: partnerships with Gymlib and Classpass, or €30/month reimbursement for your sports activities
  • Maternity/paternity leave: salary maintained at 100% during leave with no seniority requirement. Return to work at 4/5 schedule paid at 100% for 8 weeks.
  • Sustainable Mobility Package (FMD): €544.80/year (excluding full-remote contracts)
  • Meal vouchers: €10/day, 50% covered by Alma
  • Mental health: free access to MindDay platform
  • Paid time off: 25 days/year (+ additional paid leave granted for employees on executive contracts)
  • Access to our Learning & Development Platform
  • 2 weeks of full remote possible per year in summer

🎯 Interview Process

  • Video call with a Talent Acquisition team member to understand your path, motivation & present you the role.
  • Video call with Thibaut Mercier, Head of Financing, Regulatory Capital Optimization & Accounting
  • Business case
  • Video call with Stephanie Combe, CFO

🌍 Diversity & Inclusion

At Alma, we believe that diversity fuels innovation and makes our community stronger. We are committed to building a workplace where every person feels seen, respected, and empowered to do their best work whatever their gender, background, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, religion, disability or lived experience. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome applicants from all walks of life, and all employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

description:
Location: Westminster, London 

Salary: Competitive 

Reporting to: Executive Editor 

 

The Role

Reform UK is seeking an exceptional Data & Analytics Lead to build a best-in-class organisation-wide data and insight function from the party's Westminster headquarters. This is a broader opportunity than a conventional web or social analytics role: the successful candidate will help bring together disparate strands of performance, audience, membership, campaign and operational information into a coherent decision-making system.

The Data & Analytics Lead will establish the data stack, reporting definitions, access, dashboards and analytical rhythms that allow senior leaders and teams across Reform UK to see what is happening, understand why and act quickly. Digital channels will be an important part of the role, but the aim is to create a shared source of decision-ready insight across the organisation wherever useful data exists.

 

What you'll do

  • Build the organisation-wide data and insight function
  • Map the major data sources, owners, definitions, access rights, reporting rhythms and decision needs across Reform UK, identifying duplication, gaps and areas where information is currently fragmented.
  • Design and implement a practical data stack that can bring together appropriate information from digital channels, website, search, email, ReformGo, membership, campaigns and other organisational systems.
  • Establish clear definitions, baselines, targets and data-quality standards so senior leaders are not making decisions from conflicting numbers.
  • Create a roadmap that moves the organisation from isolated reports and manual extracts towards trusted, timely and increasingly automated decision support.

 

Key Responsibilities

Build dashboards that drive decisions

Create intuitive dashboards and scorecards for senior leadership and operational teams, focused on decisions rather than data for its own sake.

Develop role-appropriate views so executives can see the organisation-wide picture while teams can drill into the detail they need to manage performance day to day.

Connect output and activity to outcomes wherever attribution is reasonable, helping teams understand movement from attention to owned relationship, repeat behaviour, membership, participation or other useful actions.

Automate recurring reporting and data preparation where practical, reducing manual effort and increasing the frequency and reliability of insight.

Ensure dashboards show trends, targets and context rather than isolated totals that can easily mislead.

Turn raw data into insight and action

Produce concise, decision-ready analysis that explains what changed, why it matters, what is likely driving it and what the organisation should do next.

Identify where audiences, members or supporters stop progressing through journeys and work with relevant teams to test improvements.

Create a disciplined test-and-learn framework with hypotheses, success criteria and post-test analysis so the organisation learns systematically rather than anecdotally.

Use segmentation and cohort analysis to uncover meaningful patterns in behaviour.

Embed data-driven decision-making across Reform UK

Work with the Executive Editor, Director of Operations and other senior stakeholders to establish regular performance and insight reviews that lead to impactful decisions.

Support Website, Video, Social, Communications, Campaigns, Membership, Operations and other teams with practical analysis, helping each function understand its own performance in the wider system.

Challenge weak assumptions and vanity metrics constructively, distinguishing signal from noise and making clear where the evidence is incomplete or attribution is uncertain.

Train colleagues to understand the dashboards and core metrics so data literacy increases throughout the organisation rather than becoming dependent on one analyst.

Own governance, compliance and trust

Be the internal expert on data governance for the analytics function, ensuring work aligns with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act, ICO guidance and relevant organisational policies.

Work closely with the DPO and system owners on lawful basis, consent, minimisation, retention, access, pseudonymisation, URL/log hygiene and appropriate use of personal data.

Maintain clear data lineage, permissions and documentation so key metrics are reproducible and sensitive information is available only to those who genuinely need it.

 

Performance and Leadership:

  • Build alerting and monitoring for material changes, broken journeys, unusual movements or data-quality failures where rapid intervention is valuable.
  • Build trusted relationships with senior leaders, digital teams, campaigns, membership, operations, suppliers and technical partners so the data function is seen as an enabler rather than a reporting bottleneck.
  • Communicate complex analysis in clear, plain English, surface new ideas and be confident presenting findings to senior decision-makers.
  • Manage external analytics, BI, data or technology suppliers where required, ensuring integrations, costs and deliverables are properly controlled.
  • Maintain political awareness and discretion when working with sensitive organisational, membership or campaign data and understand that some insights will be operationally or reputationally sensitive.

 

THE PERSON

We are looking for a senior data and analytics expert who has built practical insight capability before and can turn fragmented information into a trusted system that improves decisions.

Essential experience and capabilities

  • A proven track record of establishing or materially improving a data, analytics, BI or insight operation in a complex organisation.
  • Strong experience integrating disparate data sources and designing a practical reporting architecture rather than relying on disconnected manual reports.
  • Demonstrable ability to build dashboards that colleagues actually use, with clear metrics, trends, context, drill-downs and decision relevance.
  • Excellent analytical judgement: able to distinguish signal from noise, explain uncertainty, avoid misleading attribution and turn numbers into actionable insight.
  • Strong technical competence with relevant data, analytics and BI tools, including the ability to work effectively with APIs, structured data, automation and modern dashboarding platforms.
  • Experience defining KPIs, baselines, targets, cohorts and measurement frameworks across multiple functions or stages of a user/member journey.
  • Outstanding communication skills, including the ability to explain complex analysis to non-technical senior stakeholders and influence decisions without hiding behind jargon.
  • Expert understanding of UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act, ICO guidance, consent, minimisation, retention, access controls and good data-governance practice.
  • Highly organised, self-sufficient and able to manage multiple stakeholders, systems, dependencies and priorities while maintaining clear documentation and data trust.
  • Proactive and pragmatic: willing to build a useful first version quickly, automate what matters and improve iteratively rather than waiting for a perfect enterprise architecture.
  • Strong interest in British politics and comfort handling sensitive information within a high-profile, mission-led political organisation where discretion and judgement are essential.
  • Willingness to work full-time from Reform UK's Westminster HQ and flex around major political, campaign and reporting moments when rapid analysis is required.

Highly desirable

  • Experience in political campaigning, media, membership organisations, subscriptions, CRM, advocacy or another environment where behaviour moves across multiple online and offline touchpoints.
  • Strong SQL, Python/R, data-modeling or warehouse experience and the ability to work directly with technical teams when deeper implementation is required.
  • Experience setting up experimentation, causal measurement, attribution or structured test-and-learn frameworks while communicating methodological limits clearly.
  • A track record of changing organisational behaviour through insight - for example reallocating resource, improving reach/conversion/retention, changing messaging or stopping low-value activity.

Why join Reform UK?

This is a rare opportunity to build the intelligence layer of a fast-growing national political organisation rather than inherit a narrow analytics brief. The successful candidate will bring fragmented information together and shape how senior leaders make decisions across Reform UK.

Since then, we’ve grown from 3 to 700+ people, gained unicorn status, raised ~£140M over three funding rounds, turned profitable, insured millions of drivers and lent millions in car loans. But we’re only just getting started. Our goal is to become one of the largest financial services providers in the world. Over the next 10 years we’ll grow exponentially, not only by scaling our existing products, but also by building new ones. To achieve our goals we need incredibly ambitious, commercially driven people who never settle for ‘good enough’. Marshmallowers are hungry for autonomy and ownership, and would rather improve than coast. Everyone raises standards and has an impact, with a focus on collective success over self-interest. We’ve created an environment where curious, tenacious people win and grow together. If that sounds motivating, this could be the place for you. London (hybrid, 3 days in office) Car Finance at Marshmallow Marshmallow is opening up access to credit to migrants, bringing a brand new product to market which provides newcomers to the UK with fairly priced car finance for the first time. Our Car Finance team is building a new generation lending platform from the ground up, making it simple, transparent and accessible for people who need finance to get on the road. We work closely with dealers, brokers and customers to make sure that every application, decision and interaction is fast, fair and easy to understand. Because we’re a small, high-performing team, everyone has real ownership. We combine hands-on operations with a strong focus on automation and technology. We’re designing highly automated, AI-powered processes that let us move faster and smarter than traditional lenders. The Role We're hiring a Data Scientist to sit at the heart of how we lend: who we say yes to, at what price, and how we know it's working. Our customers are people that traditional lenders struggle to assess. Many are new to the UK, have thin or no credit files, and don't fit neatly into off-the-shelf bureau scores. That makes credit decisioning at Marshmallow a genuinely hard, genuinely interesting problem: we combine bureau data, Open Banking, insurance, application and behavioural data to build a view of risk that others can't, and we need to do it in a way that is fair, explainable and compliant. This role sits between a traditional credit analyst and a data scientist. You'll build and monitor scorecards, design and test credit strategies, dig into portfolio performance to find out what's really going on, and turn large, messy datasets into insights that change how we lend. You'll own your work end-to-end: from framing the question and pulling the data through to modelling, presenting a recommendation and seeing it live in our decision engine. You'll be working with a small team and a modern stack, alongside a Head of Credit who has built this function from scratch and who will give you real ownership from day one. This is not a role where you hand models over a wall and move on - you'll see the impact of your decisions immediately. What you'll be doing Build, validate and monitor application and behavioural scorecards, using bureau, Open Banking and internal data to improve how we assess new-to-UK and thin-file customers. Design, test and refine our credit strategy: cut-offs, affordability rules, pricing tiers and limits, with a clear view of the trade-off between risk, volume and margin. Run experiments and champion/challenge tests to prove that changes to policy and models actually work before we scale them. Explore new data sources and alternative signals, and build the case for using (or not using) them in decisioning. Support model governance: document what you build, evidence that it treats customers fairly, and help us meet our Consumer Duty, CONC and model risk obligations. Work with our engineers to get models and rules into production, and use AI tooling to make yourself and the team faster. What You'll Bring Must have 2–5 years' experience in decision science or data science within consumer lending or another regulated financial services environment. Hands-on experience developing or materially refining credit scorecards or risk models (logistic regression and/or gradient boosting), including the practicalities: sample design, binning, reject inference, validation and monitoring. Experience working with Open Banking or other alternative data in credit decisioning. SQL user, and comfortable working with large, imperfect datasets. A solid grounding in statistics and a good instinct for when a result is real and when it isn't. Commercial judgement: you can translate a model output into a lending decision and explain the trade-offs to a non-technical audience. Curiosity and ownership. You ask why, you dig until you find the answer, and you'd rather ship something and improve it than wait for perfection. Nice to have Motor finance or other secured lending experience. Experience of working within a rapidly scaling lending environment. Familiarity with UK consumer credit regulation and how it shapes model design and use. Experience using LLMs to speed up analytical work. You already know some of the tooling Marshmallow uses: Snowflake, Python, Claude, Linear, Notion Perks of the job Bonus scheme designed to reward high performance Private medical insurance with Vitality, mental health support with Oliva Personal learning budget and 2 dedicated L&D days a year Monthly flexible benefits budget to spend as you choose 25 days holiday plus bank holidays 4 weeks Work From Anywhere per year We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this position. description:
Engineering Manager, Scientific Software 

(Senior Data Analyst Manager)

Do you enjoy leading engineers who turn raw scientific data into software the rest of the business can rely on? 

We're looking for an experienced Engineering Manager to lead our Data Analysis team - so named for what the product delivers to customers, though the team itself is a software and algorithm engineering team - building the applications that turn raw atomic force microscope (AFM) scan data into the 3D measurements our customers depend on. This is a pivotal role combining hands-on technical leadership with people management - shaping our software strategy and driving delivery across a growing, cross-functional organisation. Our software runs inside semiconductor fabs and processes real 3D height-profile data captured at atomic scale, so this role suits someone who enjoys working at the forefront of technology on complex problems, scientific data, and software that must be robust, reliable, and trusted by customers. 

Reward and Benefits 

  • £70,000 – £80,000 (depending on experience) 
  • Death in service and private health care benefits, discretionary annual bonus scheme and a generous EMI Share scheme 
  • Annual salary review and the opportunity to work on genuinely innovative semiconductor technology 

About the role 

You'll lead the team that builds our image-analysis application: consolidating multiple data streams from the microscope, flattening and correcting scan images, recognising scanned features and measuring their height, and running statistical analysis across large sets of measurements. Because the software runs inside a fab with no internet access, the team owns the full picture - there's no cloud service to lean on, so the algorithms, the application, and the visualisation all must hold up entirely on their own. 

Team Leadership & Delivery 

  • Leading, mentoring and developing a team of scientific software engineers, enabling them to deliver high-quality, fault-tolerant software in a time-sensitive product environment 
  • Owning the team’s software strategy, and shaping how the team works and how our image-processing algorithms, application architecture and tooling evolve 
  • Coaching team members through 1:1s, appraisals, hiring and career development 
  • Working with project leads to plan, track and report progress, and integrating the team's work into wider programme plans 
  • Managing technical debt pragmatically, balancing delivery speed against long-term maintainability 
  • Improving engineering processes so the team can keep getting better, drawing on Agile and Lean practices 

Technical Involvement 

  • Staying hands-on technically where capacity allows - reviewing code, unblocking algorithm and architecture decisions, and staying close to the data 
  • Working closely with the R&D team to translate good image processing methodology into quality product. Guiding decisions on image-processing approaches (flattening, feature recognition and masking, skew correction, height measurement etc.) and on the statistical analysis of measurement data 
  • Ensuring the application, its communication interface (over RabbitMQ) and its data visualisation are engineered to run reliably in an offline, on-premises fab environment with no cloud dependency 

Collaboration 

  • Collaborating closely with the Software Project Lead and R&D, Systems Engineering, Product and Applications teams to keep priorities aligned 
  • Managing external partners where they support delivery 

 

A note about AI: we're adopting agentic development with Claude, but our engineers retain full ownership and accountability of the code they ship - whether they wrote it or generated it. AI is a tool that amplifies engineering expertise, not a substitute for it. 

Who we are looking for 

To succeed as an Engineering Manager, Scientific Software, we do need you to bring: 

  • Experience leading and developing technical teams, including appraisals, career development and recruitment 
  • A strong, hands-on background in software development, ideally including image processing, computer vision or scientific data analysis 
  • Strong Python development skills with industry experience 
  • Practical experience using Agile and Lean methodologies 
  • Good understanding of the software development lifecycle and best practice 
  • Experience working with external partners or suppliers 
  • Project management experience 
  • Clear communication skills in English, and a collaborative, pragmatic, self-motivated approach 
  • 5+ years’ experience in software development, and 5+ years' experience in technical leadership or people management 

Nice to have 

  • Experience developing software for processing and visualising 3D imaging or scientific data 
  • Background in metrology, microscopy, semiconductors or other complex engineering products 
  • Experience from another scientific or technical discipline, backed by strong software experience 
  • Experience using AI-assisted or agentic coding tools (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Claude Code) to improve development speed and quality in a professional setting 

A bit about us: 

Infinitesima is a privately owned company founded in 2001, as a spin-out of the University of Bristol, by CTO Professor Andrew Humphris. Our dynamic team of scientists and engineers is focussed on enabling the next generation of semiconductor devices through delivery of innovative products to customers around the world. 

Our strength lies in the varied perspectives that come from different cultures, experiences, and identities. We believe that true innovation is fuelled by collaboration, locally and globally. We strive to foster an environment where everyone can contribute meaningfully and thrive. If you require adjustments to take part in the recruitment process, please let us know, we’ll do our best to support you.

Your recruitment journey:

We will interview you: Monday to Friday UK Time 9am to 4.30pm and we'll be as flexible as we can with Global Scheduling

1st stage: (45 minute) Remote meeting to evaluate your experience and technical ability

2nd stage: (2.5 hours) Face to face onsite evaluating technical, presentation and communication skills along with your ways of working and your opportunity to to know more about us

If you're not comfortable with eye contact, let us know at the start of your interview and if REMOTE, once we've said hello, feel free to turn your camera off until the end.

We dress casually so informal attire is absolutely fine for onsite interviews. We want you to feel comfortable when you meet us and if there's anything else we can do to support your journey, just let us know. 

A note on how we use AI:
We use AI only to transcribe our interviews so we can focus fully on you instead of scribbling notes. The AI does not take part in any decision making at any stage. All hiring decisions are made by real humans based on the conversation we have with you.

Location and working pattern:

We offer flexible, hybrid working from day one, where possible. During your first three months with us, we ask for 4 days per week on site here at Abingdon, with 1 day remote. After probation, this typically settles to around a 3:2 split between office and remote working. 

Recruitment agencies: Infinitesima Ltd only works with approved agencies and does not accept unsolicited agency CVs. Please do not submit candidate details in response to this advert or solicit any Infinitesima Ltd employees. Infinitesima Ltd is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited CVs.

description:
🧡 About Alma

At Alma, we believe sustainable commerce depends on fair, well‑balanced trade. Because finance plays a pivotal role in business, our mission is to put it back in its rightful place - serving merchants and consumers.

Our installment and deferred payment solutions help merchants boost sales by 20% or more, increase customer loyalty, and deliver a seamless shopping experience - without encouraging bad debt.

As the buy now pay later leader in France and active in 10 European countries, we've empowered over +25,000 merchants and 10 million consumers.

With 400+ Almakers and €100M+ ARR, Alma is scaling rapidly across Europe as a member of the Next40, and we're just getting started!

👐 About the team

The Head of Legal supports Alma to grow safely and sustainably by anticipating and managing legal risk, providing pragmatic advice, negotiating contracts, and supporting teams across the company; in a strongly regulated environment.

The Head of Legal reports to Alma’s General Secretary and lead the Legal function. You will be a trusted partner to the Director’s Committee and work closely with Product, Tech, Sales, Operations, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Information Security and People.

You will also act as Alma’s Data Protection Officer, with the independence, resources and direct access to senior management required to perform the role effectively.

This is a permanent position based in Paris.

💼 About the job

As Head of Legal, you will define Alma’s legal and privacy strategy and ensure that it supports the company’s business ambitions, regulatory obligations and risk appetite.

Your main responsibilities will include:

Define and lead Alma’s legal strategy

  • Develop and execute a clear legal roadmap aligned with Alma’s business and international strategy.
  • Identify, assess and manage Alma’s main legal risks, escalating material matters to executive management and governance bodies when appropriate.
  • Provide clear, pragmatic and business-oriented advice to the Executive Committee and teams across Alma.
  • Translate complex legal requirements into actionable recommendations, policies and scalable operational processes.
  • Monitor relevant legal developments across Alma’s markets and anticipate their impact on the company’s products and activities.

Support Alma’s business, products and partnerships

  • Advise Product and Tech teams throughout the design and launch of new products and features, embedding legal and privacy considerations from the outset.
  • Support Sales, Account Management, Operations and other business teams on strategic projects and complex legal questions.
  • Oversee the drafting, review and negotiation of commercial agreements, including agreements with merchants, partners, suppliers and technology providers.
  • Establish scalable contracting standards, templates, playbooks and approval processes that enable teams to move quickly while controlling legal risk.
  • Advise on strategic transactions, partnerships, outsourcing arrangements and international expansion projects.

Oversee corporate and governance matters

  • Manage Alma’s corporate legal matters and ensure that its legal entities comply with applicable governance and corporate requirements.
  • Support executive management and governance bodies in preparing decisions and maintaining appropriate corporate documentation.
  • Advise on financing, corporate transactions, intellectual property, competition law and other strategic legal matters.
  • Coordinate external counsel and manage the legal budget, ensuring that external expertise is used effectively.
  • Oversee litigation, pre-litigation, claims and other disputes, defining the appropriate strategy and protecting Alma’s interests.

Act as Alma’s Data Protection Officer

  • Define and oversee Alma’s data protection framework in accordance with the GDPR and other applicable privacy laws.
  • Inform and advise Alma and its employees on their data protection obligations.
  • Monitor compliance through appropriate policies, processes, controls and reporting.
  • Maintain and continuously improve Alma’s privacy governance, including records of processing activities, privacy notices, retention standards and procedures for handling data-subject requests.
  • Establish a robust framework for data protection impact assessments and ensure that DPIAs are conducted when required.
  • Advise Product, Tech, Data, Risk, Operations, Marketing and People teams on privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default principles.
  • Work closely with Information Security on personal-data breaches, incident response, security measures and regulatory notifications.
  • Act as Alma’s primary contact for data protection authorities and cooperate with them when required.
  • Develop training and awareness initiatives to foster a strong data protection culture throughout Alma.

Lead and develop the Legal team

  • Set a clear vision, priorities and operating model for the Legal team.
  • Manage, coach and develop team members, promoting high standards of expertise, ownership and collaboration.
  • Allocate resources according to business priorities and ensure that legal requests are handled effectively.
  • Define meaningful objectives and indicators to measure the team’s impact, service quality and risk management.
  • Build trusted relationships across Alma and position Legal as both a strategic partner and an independent control function.

🧩 About you

You combine excellent legal judgment with a strong understanding of business. You are comfortable taking clear positions on complex matters while remaining pragmatic and solution-oriented.

You are likely to thrive in this role if you:

  • Can move comfortably between strategic questions and hands-on legal work.
  • Understand how to balance business velocity, customer experience, innovation and legal risk.
  • Communicate complex legal matters clearly to both legal and non-legal audiences.
  • Build trusted relationships with senior leaders and challenge decisions constructively when necessary.
  • Enjoy developing people and creating clarity for a multidisciplinary team.
  • Are comfortable working with incomplete information and taking ownership of sensitive or high-impact decisions.
  • Have strong negotiation, drafting and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Are fluent in both French and English.

Your experience

  • You hold a Master’s degree in law or an equivalent legal qualification.
  • You have significant experience in senior legal positions (15+ years), combining experience in a leading bank or FinTech and a law firm.
  • You have strong expertise in banking, commercial and technology contracts, corporate matters and business law.
  • Experience supporting international activities and working across several European jurisdictions would also be valuable.
  • You have the level of expertise and professional standing required to act as Data Protection Officer.

Hiring process

Because of the strategic importance of this role, the recruitment process will be thorough while remaining as efficient as possible. It is expected to include:

  1. An introductory conversation with the Talent Acquisition team.
  2. An interview with the General Secretary.
  3. A practical case study focused on legal strategy, business partnering and data protection with key members of the team.
  4. Meetings with key members of Alma’s leadership and relevant cross-functional stakeholders.
  5. An interview with one of our co-founders.

🌍 Diversity & Inclusion

At Alma, we believe that diversity fuels innovation and makes our community stronger. We are committed to building a workplace where every person feels seen, respected, and empowered to do their best work whatever their gender, background, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, religion, disability or lived experience. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome applicants from all walks of life, and all employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

description: Description Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale. We set the standard for AI-powered contract review. Today we build a holistic platform that changes how legal teams operate from review to negotiation, powered by our Legal Agent. We are looking for the person who makes that value real for customers: in the demo, in onboarding, and inside the AI itself. When you join Legartis, you don't just take a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and legal experts. We don't chase hype; we build substance. Your mission This is not a classic legal role, and not a classic sales or product role. You operate at the intersection of Law, Revenue, and AI, where you are a lever, not a bottleneck: your job is to build the demos, playbooks, and standards that let the whole company scale, and to step into the calls where your expertise closes the gap. 1. Commercial impact. You help win and grow customers. You build and run demos that create a "wow" moment, join high-stakes prospect calls as the legal expert who speaks at eye level with GCs, and run our trials and workshops: onboarding sessions where customers solve their own use cases live, with you coaching. You turn objections into use cases and interest into next steps, and you enable our Sales team to tell the legal story without you in the room. You think of outcomes in terms of trial-to-signature conversion, adoption, expansion. 2. Customer transformation. Once a deal is signed, you make the value real by acting as a strategic sparring partner in onboarding: defining review requirements, tuning playbooks and prompts, and showing legal teams where Legartis delivers the highest ROI. You turn individual learnings into scalable standards and documentation. 3. Making the AI better. You work hands-on with the Legal Agent: prompting, testing, diagnosing where it breaks and why. You feed what you learn from customers back into Product and Engineering (playbook quality, test sets, edge cases) so the product improves with every customer. 4. Internal legal support. You don't just sell the tool; you use it. When necessary, you support Legartis as in-house counsel on contract reviews and specific legal questions. Your profile We are honest: people who combine all of this are rare. We hire for aptitude and attitude, assess hands-on in a case study, and train the rest side by side, in real customer work. 1. You can sell the product (key). Not in the cold-calling sense, but in the way a great expert sells: by making the customer succeed in front of their own team. Concretely, this means you can (or want to learn to): Run a live demo with confidence including customized, high-stakes demos and recover gracefully when something doesn't land: pull out a better prompt, adjust on the spot, turn a skeptical question into a stronger result. Coach the customer hands-on. In trials and hackathons, the customer drives and you navigate: you get them to enter their own real legal questions, create the first "wow" moment themselves, and build the habits (saved prompts, reusable workflows) that make them stay. Turn objections into use cases. When a customer says "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves," you respond with a concrete path: a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative. You're straight about limits, because credibility is what closes. Speak at eye level with GCs and legal teams asking sharp discovery questions, translating their friction points into what the product can do, and framing value in their language (ROI, risk, time saved). Always leave with a next step. Trial licenses, a hackathon, a follow-up workshop, a scoped rollout conversation. You instinctively convert interest into momentum, and you remove friction ("we can make that happen") rather than adding process. Ideally you can point to moments where you influenced a deal, a renewal, or an expansion in any prior role. 2. Legal foundation. Solid legal training and hands-on experience with commercial contracts from in-house, law firm, or legal tech. Optical & Semiconductor Systems

£33,000 to £40,000 depending on experience

Help build the technology enabling the next generation of semiconductors.

At Infinitesima, we're developing advanced metrology systems that allow the world's leading semiconductor companies to measure and understand materials at the nanoscale.

We're looking for a skilled Manufacturing Technician to build, integrate and test the high-precision optical, electro-mechanical and photonic systems that sit at the heart of our technology.

This is an opportunity to join a fast-growing technology company where your work has a direct impact on the performance of complex scientific instruments used by global semiconductor manufacturers.

If you enjoy solving problems, working with precision hardware and taking ownership of build quality from assembly through to test, we'd love to hear from you.

What you'll get

  • Generous EMI share option scheme
  • Private healthcare
  • Death in service benefit

About us

Based in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, Infinitesima is a rapidly growing deep-tech company developing next-generation metrology solutions for the semiconductor industry.

Backed by leading global investors, including Applied Ventures, we're combining world-class engineering, physics and software expertise to solve some of the industry's most complex measurement challenges.

What you'll be doing

  • Manufacture and test complex sub-assemblies involving optical, cabling, and electro-mechanical technologies, ensuring compliance with quality and performance standards.
  • Identify, document, and escalate manufacturing issues—including defects, downtime, and abnormalities—using factual information, while collaborating with cross-functional support teams to drive timely and effective resolution.
  • Working as a manufacturing team in maintaining and continuously improving manufacturing processes to enhance product quality and operational efficiency.
  • Ensuring assemblies are delivered to quality, cost and schedule requirements
  • Maintain high standards of housekeeping and cleanliness across production and cleanroom environments.
  • Liaise with Stock Operatives to ensure assembly kits are complete & accurate.
  • Contributing to a safe, organised and high-performing manufacturing environment

What we're looking for

You'll ideally come from semiconductor equipment, photonics, scientific instrumentation, aerospace, medical devices or another high-tech manufacturing environment.

We'd particularly like to hear from people with experience of:

  • Building and testing complex, high-value technology products
  • Electro-mechanical assembly and system integration
  • Root cause analysis and structured problem solving
  • Manufacturing practice, quality standards and root-cause basics
  • Reading and following technical documentation and build procedures
  • Working with precision mechanical and electronic components
  • Strong attention to detail and pride in workmanship

Nice to have

  • Semiconductor equipment or semiconductor manufacturing experience
  • Cleanroom working experience
  • Wiring and soldering to IPC standards
  • Experience working with complex photonics or metrology equipment, such as optical systems, lasers, fibre optics, and precision instrumentation.
  • Manufacturing engineering or process improvement exposure

A bit about us: 

Infinitesima is a privately owned company founded in 2001, as a spin-out of the University of Bristol, by CTO Professor Andrew Humphris. Our dynamic team of scientists and engineers is focussed on enabling the next generation of semiconductor devices through delivery of innovative products to customers around the world. 

Our strength lies in the varied perspectives that come from different cultures, experiences, and identities. We believe that true innovation is fuelled by collaboration, locally and globally. We strive to foster an environment where everyone can contribute meaningfully and thrive. If you require adjustments to take part in the recruitment process, please let us know, we’ll do our best to support you.

Your recruitment journey:

We will interview you: Monday to Friday UK Time 9am to 4.30pm and we'll be as flexible as we can with Global Scheduling

1st stage: (45 minute) Remote meeting to evaluate your experience and technical ability

2nd stage: (2.5 hours) Face to face onsite evaluating technical, presentation and communication skills along with your ways of working and your opportunity to to know more about us

If you're not comfortable with eye contact, let us know at the start of your interview and if REMOTE, once we've said hello, feel free to turn your camera off until the end.

Informal dress is absolutely fine for onsite interviews, we want you to feel comfortable when you meet us and if there's anything else we can do to support your journey, just let us know. 

A note on how we use AI:
We use AI only to transcribe our interviews so we can focus fully on you instead of scribbling notes. The AI does not take part in any decision making at any stage. All hiring decisions are made by real humans based on the conversation we have with you.

Location and working pattern:
This roles requires onsite attendance Monday to Friday.

Recruitment agencies: Infinitesima Ltd only works with approved agencies and does not accept unsolicited agency CVs. Please do not submit candidate details in response to this advert or solicit any Infinitesima Ltd employees. Infinitesima Ltd is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited CVs.

Capco est un cabinet de conseil international, spécialisé dans les services financiers.

LOCATION & TRAVEL

description:
Castrol is one of the world’s leading lubricant brands, serving customers and consumers in the automotive, marine, industrial and energy sectors. Castrol brands are recognised globally for their premium quality and high performance, shaped by the company’s commitment to innovation and cutting-edge technology. With products sold in more than 150 countries, Castrol has helped keep things moving on roads and racetracks, air, sea, and space for over 125 years. 

Whether you're just starting out or ready for your next big move, you're in the right place to explore an exciting career with Castrol.

 

Job description

About the team

You'll join Castrol's Global Pricing team, reporting to the Global Strategic Pricing Manager and leading a small team of data scientists and analysts. Working alongside colleagues with pricing and commercial expertise, you'll combine technical problem-solving with developing others, turning your team's analysis into decisions that improve revenue, margin and product mix.

Key tasks

Which pricing questions are worth solving, and how do you turn the answers into something the business can use? You'll help connect the commercial problem, the analytical approach and the practical solution.

  • Find where margin is being lost across discounts, rebates and trade investments. Quantify the opportunity, recommend corrective action and support governance of pricing corridors, floors and exceptions.
  • Help the business make better product-price-pack and portfolio choices across DIY, DIFM and B2B channels. Explore customers, segments, specifications, pack sizes and tiers to inform price positioning and the price steps between offerings.
  • Develop and deploy models for elasticity, demand forecasting, willingness to pay, price sensitivity, scenarios and price optimisation, translating the results into recommendations people can act on.
  • Turn recurring work into repeatable tools. Design automation for price changes, analysis, reporting and decision support, reducing manual intervention and making solutions usable across markets.
  • Lead and develop your analytical team, encouraging commercial curiosity and innovation. Set priorities around business value, plan projects and help colleagues turn their technical work into practical outcomes.
  • Partner with Pricing, Sales, Finance and Marketing, using clear explanations of the evidence to influence senior stakeholders and connect analytical findings to commercial decisions.

Success means more than delivering a model: it means measurable commercial impact, pricing processes that need less manual effort, and a team that understands its priorities and develops its capabilities.

Experience required

You don't need a long management career behind you. You'll need technical depth, evidence that your analysis makes a difference, and the aptitude to help others do their best work.

  • A university degree or higher, with proven experience in pricing analytics, data science or operations research, ideally in a commercial environment.
  • Strong mathematical and statistical modelling skills, including regression, machine learning and segmentation, and the ability to apply them to questions such as demand forecasting, elasticity and price optimisation.
  • Proficiency in analytical tools such as Python, R and SQL and visualisation platforms such as Power BI or Tableau, with experience working with large datasets and building scalable solutions.
  • Evidence of translating analysis into business impact, supported by commercial judgement, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
  • The ability and aptitude to lead and develop a small analytical team. Previous leadership or mentoring experience is valuable, but strong technical candidates with less management experience will also be considered.
  • Experience delivering and leading projects, with the initiative, planning, prioritisation and collaborative approach needed to keep work moving.
  • Fluent written and spoken English, with the ability to explain complex findings, influence stakeholders at different levels and build relationships within and beyond Global Pricing.
  • Desirable: pricing or revenue growth management experience, including gross-to-net, trade spend and portfolio/mix optimisation. Strong transferable data science or operations research experience is welcome, with scope to learn the pricing domain; exposure to automation tools and workflows is highly desirable.

Privacy

The Castrol entity recruiting for this role is the data controller for the personal information you provide. We use it to assess your application and to manage the recruitment and onboarding process. We may share it with service providers who support our recruitment, and it may be transferred to other Castrol entities internationally under appropriate safeguards. We keep it only for as long as necessary. For details of how we use your information and your data protection rights, contact We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, socioeconomic status, neurodiversity/neurocognitive functioning, veteran status or disability status. Individuals with an accessibility need may request an adjustment/accommodation related to Castrol recruiting process (e.g., accessing the job application, completing required assessments, participating in telephone screenings or interviews, etc.).

If you are selected for a position and depending upon your role, your employment may be contingent upon adherence to local policy. This may include pre-placement drug screening, medical review of physical fitness for the role, and background checks.
